newsitem.title: UK: Six held in IRA bomb probe - security sources.
newsitem.headline: Six held in IRA bomb probe - security sources.

text.p: Northern Ireland police investigating an upsurge in IRA guerrilla violence were questioning six men on Friday, British security sources said.

They said the detainees were being quizzed about an Irish Republican Army double car bomb that killed a soldier in the province's main army garrison in October, and a rocket attack on Monday on Belfast's main law courts.
"We can confirm that a number of people are being questioned about serious crime in the Greater Belfast area," a spokesman for the Royal Ulster Constabulary police said.
The October attack on Thiepval Barracks in Lisburn marked the extension to the province of an IRA bombing wave that since last February had been concentrated on English cities.
A police officer was slightly hurt on Monday when a guerrilla missile hit a security hut at the entrance to the Courts of Justice in Belfast.

A spate of attacks and botched raids by the IRA has prompted fears that the province could slide back into the cycle of sectarian warfare that scarred it for 27 years until twin truces by the IRA and its pro-British Loyalist guerrilla foes.

Loyalist guerrillas have been blamed for two recent bomb attacks on leading Irish republicans in Belfast and Londonderry city. Loyalist politicians insist that a 26-month truce by Protestant extremists is still operating.

The IRA, fighting a war to end British rule of Northern Ireland, abandoned a 17-month truce in February. Britain says the IRA must declare a second ceasefire before its political wing Sinn Fein is given a seat in all-party talks on the province's future.
